label: first copy step after <DEL> echoing "w" (long sequences, L>=6)
explanation: Fires almost only at the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, t = L+1), when the input is the model fed-back first output, the letter w (so the first original token was w), and only for sequences with L >= 6. It never fires for L <= 5 or on any other copy position, and essentially never in the original or delimiter phases (3 stray activations). Magnitude grows with L: L=6 sequences carry about 4% of the activation mass and L=8-9 most of it. Lowest-quartile examples are mostly L=6-7. The token being output (orig(1)) has no clear effect on magnitude. A handful of activations come from other fed-back first tokens (d, t, k, c).

issues: Every false positive (about 487 on test) is at L=6. For L=6 alone the predicate has precision 0.82. For L>=7 it has precision 1.0, with F1 0.88 and mass recall 0.957. The L=6 false positives show no pattern in later tokens, so they look like the feature falling below threshold at its weakest length, which fits the explanation's point that magnitude grows with L. It is not a separate class of counterexamples.

The 59 missed activations hold 0.0% of the mass. Most are tiny activations (0.01-0.06) at recall_idx 1 when orig(0)=d or c and orig(1)=w (w is the second original token). The rest are stray original-phase activations on w at the step just before <DEL>. All of these are negligible.

Claims checked: 100% of the mass is at recall_idx 1. There are zero activations for L<=5 and 3 stray ones in the original phase. Mass shares by L are 0.043, 0.215, 0.346 and 0.396 for L=6 to 9. Dropping L>=6 gives precision 0.630, which matches the reported 0.63. The output token's class barely matters (digits 0.93 precision, vowels 0.98).
